commands.review_summary:
The branch rewrites shared Apple chat recovery to adopt `chat.history.inFlightRun` snapshots after reconnect, foreground resume, and event gaps, while preserving Gateway user idempotency in Codex/Copilot transcript mirrors.

PR surface: Source +53, Tests +83, Docs +1, Other +1505. Total +1642 across 23 files.

Reproducibility: yes. source inspection shows current main exposes `chat.history.inFlightRun` on the Gateway but the Apple history payload did not decode it, and foreground recovery only refreshed when a local pending run already existed. The PR also includes live simulator proof of the reconnect recovery path.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] The remaining action is maintainer land judgment plus release-owned changelog cleanup, not a safe autonomous repair lane because the PR carries the protected maintainer label and touches session/message recovery semantics.

target.title: fix(ios): restore in-flight runs after reconnect
target.body:
Part of #100197. Supersedes the stacked `afterSeq` design in #100267.

## What Problem This Solves

When iOS backgrounds, reconnects, changes sessions, or misses an event sequence, it can lose ownership of a run that is still active on the Gateway. The transcript may look idle, Abort disappears, and a second send becomes possible while the first run is still working.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already exposes the canonical active-run snapshot through `chat.history.inFlightRun`; the TUI already consumes that contract. This rewrite removes every proposed `afterSeq` protocol/client change and restores ownership from the existing snapshot instead.

The shared Apple chat model now:

- adopts active run ID and buffered text during bootstrap, foreground resume, sequence-gap recovery, immediate post-send refresh, delayed retries, and completion refreshes;
- orders history snapshots against newer live deltas, terminal events, session messages, session switches, agent changes, and concurrent history requests;
- keeps ownership stable when another client streams a different run in the same session;
- scopes bare-global/default-agent aliases and non-default agent-qualified global sessions without cross-agent transcript adoption;
- keeps the chat transport unscoped until Gateway metadata resolves the real default agent, then rebuilds even when the visible fallback remains `main`;
- distinguishes current Gateway negative state via `sessionInfo.hasActiveRun` from legacy gateways that omit active-run metadata;
- preserves live/provisional transcript rows when delayed history arrives, including identical replies from different turns;
- rearms timeouts safely and clears silent completed/failed runs from authoritative current-Gateway state.
- preserves the foreground completion haptic when the authoritative recovery snapshot clears a pending run.

The provider transcript mirrors now preserve the Gateway-owned user idempotency key. Codex and Copilot still attach their provider-specific mirror identity, but no longer replace the canonical `<runId>:user` identity or let mirrored prompts participate in stale failed-run binding recovery. This gives history reconciliation one stable user-turn boundary across optimistic UI, Gateway history, and provider transcript storage.

Codex app-server source confirms a turn becomes `InProgress` with no message items before later `AgentMessageDelta` notifications (`codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:155`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/event_mapping.rs:359`). That is why an active run with an empty buffered string is still valid ownership.

## User Impact

Returning to iOS or macOS chat no longer loses an active response. Streaming text, tool state, Abort, and the send lock recover without adding a Gateway protocol or cursor, while older Gateways retain the prior transcript-based completion fallback.

## Evidence

- `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter ChatViewModelTests` — 136/136 passed, including duplicate finals, repeated identical turns, incomplete history, canonical provider adoption, and discarded-view-model listener lifetime.
- Blacksmith Testbox `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/transcript-mirror.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts` — 134/134 passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox `pnpm test extensions/copilot/src/dual-write-transcripts.test.ts extensions/copilot/src/attempt.test.ts` — 129/129 passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwt13g1jy7ast7t6zsdz1myn` changed gate — passed on range-diff-identical rebased head `b4bfadffab9`: extension/test typechecks, oxlint, Apple app lane, macOS CI tests, DB-first guard, sidecar guard, and import-cycle guard.
- Exact-head hosted CI run `28755490196` — passed, including iOS/macOS builds, native i18n, lint, type/boundary/dependency guards, Android, Node shards, and QA Smoke.
- Functional-tree iOS Simulator build, install, and launch on iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5 — passed; exact-head hosted iOS build also passed.
- Live range-diff-identical Gateway + simulator recovery — one optimistic user row before backgrounding; foreground history restored `Writing` and Stop; completion reconciled to one user row and one `RECOVERY_FINAL_EXACT_100277` assistant row.
- Persisted live transcript — Gateway user key remained `<runId>:user`; Codex mirror metadata remained separately marked `mirrorOrigin=codex-app-server`.
- SwiftFormat lint with `config/swiftformat` — clean for every touched Swift file.
- Final full-branch Codex autoreview — clean; no accepted/actionable findings.
- Exact final head: `fb4a3551c7855cb361dc201e81a482a6a2773c66`; fresh autoreview was clean on range-diff-identical head `b4bfadffab9`.
- Direct Gateway contract review: `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts`, `src/gateway/server-session-events.ts`, and `src/gateway/server-methods/session-active-runs.ts`.
- Direct Codex contract review at `be33f80bc65159c094ecd06bf155afa3061ce23d`: `codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:155-183`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/event_mapping.rs:359-367`, and `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs:375-378`.
